criteria.criterion: Navigate Xbox.com to the 'Best sellers' section
criteria.final_justification: The action history suggests the agent intended to reach Best sellers, but the visual evidence does not corroborate that the agent actually located a “Best sellers” section (or even a clearly best-selling list) before opening the product page. With no blocker shown, this is an evidentiary gap; award partial credit for reasonable navigation attempt (home → games) but not full credit for successfully finding the Best sellers section.

criteria.criterion: Open a product page for a game from 'Best sellers'
criteria.final_justification: It is confirmed the agent opened a valid Xbox.com product page, satisfying the core of opening a product page. However, because the screenshots never show the game being selected from a “Best sellers” section, traceability to that required section is not visually verified. Per rubric, this merits partial credit rather than full.

criteria.criterion: Report publisher, developer, and release date from the product page
criteria.final_justification: The page does contain all required information, but the agent’s final output omits the publisher and explicitly (and incorrectly) states it cannot be verified, contradicting the screenshot. Developer and release date were correctly captured. This is a substantive omission/contradiction for 1 of 3 required fields, so award strong partial credit but not full.

criteria.criterion: Respect constraints (no sign-in; no purchase or download; stop after recording details)
criteria.final_justification: Constraints appear respected (no sign-in, no purchase/download). The agent did stop without further actions beyond viewing/scrolling, though it failed to record the publisher despite it being available; that affects Criterion 2, not constraint compliance. Full credit.
